source: data/deep statements — q-0009 left-truncation caveat audit
caveat_audited: e-0017/e-0020/e-0024 all soften their pessimistic section-predictor learnability findings by asserting 'statements are left-truncated, so a real transformer sees more'. This quantifies how much is actually lost.

LEFT_TRUNCATED.note: detected via running bracket depth going negative; a lower bound (bracket-free lost prefixes are invisible).

truncated_whose_surviving_tail_has_libra.note: library content lives in TYPES (preserved after the cut names), not in the lost binder names.

truncated_with_INTACT_conclusion(balance.note: the conclusion — the predictor's key input — survives.

interpretation: Truncation is DOMINANT (88.6%) but SHALLOW: 99.6% lose exactly one leading binder group (depth -1), the cut sits at the binder-name boundary (short surviving type tail), and the full conclusion + all hypotheses after the first group survive (99.6% intact conclusions). The lost material is one binder group's NAMES (lowercase locals); library/content vocabulary lives in the preserved types and conclusion. So the e-0020/e-0024 'lower bound, transformer sees more' escape hatch is bounded to one binder group's names — it cannot rescue the 37.5%-grounding / no-width-prediction findings by much. q-0009's learnability concern stands close to face value.
